title: Pressure-cooker chickpeas from dried
subtitle: Tender, flavourful chickpeas without any soaking
excerpt: Dried chickpeas cooked from scratch under pressure in about 45 minutes. No overnight soak, better flavour than tinned, and a starchy cooking liquid that works as vegetable stock.
sourceNotes: Pressure-cooking chickpeas from dried is the standard method in Indian, Middle Eastern, and Spanish home cooking where chickpea dishes are made regularly from bulk dried stock. The no-soak method is documented in electric pressure cooker and pressure-cooker guides throughout the 2010s.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze in portions in their cooking liquid for up to 6 months. Defrost overnight in the fridge.
recipe.batchNotes: Cook a large batch and freeze in 400 g portions equivalent to one tin. Use straight from frozen in soups.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Cooked chickpeas keep refrigerated in their cooking liquid for up to 5 days.

content.text: Chickpeas cooked from dried in a pressure cooker are noticeably better than tinned: fuller in flavour, more robustly textured, and free of the slight metallic edge that can come with tinned legumes. The chickpeas take about 45 minutes at high pressure from dry, no soaking needed.

The cooking liquid is aquafaba, the starchy, protein-rich water that can be used as an egg-white substitute in baking, or simply used as a flavoured stock in soups and stews. It is worth keeping rather than discarding.
As with all dried beans, do not add salt or acidic ingredients until the chickpeas are fully cooked. Both toughen the skins and slow down the process significantly.

Put the rinsed chickpeas in the pressure cooker. Cover with cold water by at least 7 cm, chickpeas expand significantly and absorb water. Add the garlic, bay leaf, and olive oil. Do not add salt. Seal the lid and bring to high pressure. Cook at high pressure for 45 minutes. Allow a full natural pressure release, about 20 minutes.

Open the lid and taste a chickpea, it should be tender throughout with a creamy interior and no chalky bite. If still firm, return to high pressure for a further 15 minutes. Once cooked, season generously with salt and stir through. Cool in the liquid before using, refrigerating, or freezing.

rows.symptom: The chickpeas are still firm after 45 minutes
rows.cause: Old chickpeas, or chickpeas stored in damp conditions, take longer to cook.
rows.fix: Cook for a further 15 to 20 minutes at high pressure. If still firm, the dried beans are very old, use this batch for hummus where the texture matters less.

rows.symptom: The chickpeas are very soft and starting to break apart
rows.fix: Use this batch for hummus or mashing into dips. For next time, reduce by 5 minutes and use natural release.

rows.symptom: Foam is coming from the pressure release valve
rows.cause: Legumes produce foam and the cooker may be overfilled.
rows.fix: Never fill the pressure cooker more than half full when cooking dried legumes, they expand significantly and the foam can block the valve.

content.text: Home-cooked chickpeas are a starting point for many dishes: hummus, chana masala, shakshuka, pasta e ceci, roasted chickpea salads, and simple soups. A batch cooked once a week and kept in the fridge replaces the constant stream of opened tins. The cooking liquid is usable wherever stock or a thickener is needed, and in meringue-style baking as a direct egg-white substitute.
